evidence.supports: Confirms the first of two required public hearings occurred 2026-09-22 with no vote taken, the second hearing date (Oct. 27), and the possible early-December final-consideration timeline.
evidence.quote: The Denton City Council held the first of two required public hearings on the proposed moratorium. No vote was taken on Tuesday. The second hearing is scheduled for Oct. 27. ... City officials have outlined a process that could bring the proposal back to the council for final consideration in early December.

evidence.supports: Confirms the Council's initial vote to start the legal process required before a moratorium can be adopted, requiring two public hearings first.
evidence.quote: Denton City Council voted to start the legal process toward a possible moratorium on data centers. Two public hearings must be held before council members can vote on the resolution.

decisions.notes: Verified: first of two required hearings held Sept. 22, 2026, no vote taken, second hearing Oct. 27, 2026. 'pending' correct.

evidence.supports: Detailed account of the Aug. 11, 2026 Council action (three measures, near-unanimous votes), the required remaining hearings, and city staff's projected timeline for when a moratorium (if adopted) would actually begin and end.
evidence.quote: If the council approves the moratorium by supermajority, it could begin in February and end in May with the option to extend it for an additional 90 days into August. ... The initial 90-day moratorium would end on May 17, with an option to extend it until Aug. 15.

evidence.supports: Confirms the Aug. 11, 2026 Council vote created the Data Center & Infrastructure Commission the same meeting it began the moratorium process, and that the commission's report is due by the Nov. 3, 2026 work session.
evidence.quote: This comes after Fort Worth City Council formed and voted for the commission Aug. 11, the same meeting in which they voted to begin the process of a data center moratorium. ... The group is also expected to deliver a report of recommendations to the council by their Nov. 3 work session.

evidence.supports: Confirms, as of the day before this research date, that the city is still only 'considering' the 90-day moratorium and has not adopted it.
evidence.quote: On Aug. 11, the city began considering a 90-day moratorium on the construction of new data centers while they study and prepare for possible regulations.

decisions.notes: Verified: Aug. 11, 2026 Council action only began the statutory process; three independent Sept. 2026 sources confirm no moratorium is in place yet. 'pending' correct, and the projected Feb.-Aug. 2027 window (if adopted) is properly framed as conditional.

evidence.supports: Confirms the 5-2 vote, the dissenting councilmembers' reasoning, the citizen petition origin, the 90-day proposal (with optional 90-day extension), and that this is a resolution starting the process rather than an adopted moratorium.
evidence.quote: The resolution to start the moratorium process was approved 5-2. ... If the optional 90-day moratorium extension were to be approved by council, a potential large-scale data center would not be considered until June of 2027.

decisions.notes: Verified against KCBD: 5-2 vote on 2026-09-23 (the research date itself) to start the process; not an adopted moratorium. 'pending' correct.
